title: Nvidia Is Going to Space With Elon Musk's Million-Satellites Plan. Here's Why It Could Be the Start of a Trillion-Dollar Cycle.
excerpt: SpaceX’s exclusive commitment to Nvidia signals the chipmaker’s AI leadership is expanding into entirely new markets.
content_html:
Jabran Kundi

Sun, August 9, 2026 at 1:11 PM PDT 6 min read

Nvidia (NVDA) just extended its grip on artificial intelligence (AI) computing with plans to go where no chipmaker has gone before: orbit. On Aug. 4, SpaceX (SPCX) and Nvidia announced they are partnering to design the compute payload for the Starmind AI1 satellite, which will run heavy AI workloads from space using Nvidia's newest hardware. The plan is not a one-off. SpaceX has outlined a long-term vision that could eventually scale to as many 1 million AI satellites. Together, these satellites would work as one giant data center circling the Earth.

Even more than the spectacle, what stands out for Nvidia is the commitment behind this partnership. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said bluntly that the company has agreed to exclusively use Nvidia GPUs because "the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture." That is about as strong an endorsement as it gets, especially because it comes from the one customer with every reason to build his own chips or look for alternatives.

Why This Matters for Nvidia

This deal also shows how fast Nvidia's newest push is gaining ground. When the company launched its space computing platform back in March, it named six partners, and SpaceX was not one of them. After just a few months, the most ambitious space company in the world has now signed on as well.

The hardware at the center of this news is Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform. The company says it delivers up to 25 times the AI performance of its H100 chips in orbit. This matters because the opportunity could be enormous. Futurum Research estimates orbital computing could become a $1 trillion market by 2030, driven by falling Starship launch costs and the power limits choking data centers on the ground. If that plays out, Nvidia is positioned as a prime beneficiary.

The logic behind moving compute to space is more practical than it sounds. AI data centers on Earth are running into hard limits on power, land, and cooling. In orbit, satellites get constant solar energy and natural cooling for free, avoiding the very bottlenecks holding back data centers on Earth.

For Nvidia investors, the near-term payoff is small. Space chips ship only later this year, and a 1-million-satellite network is a long way off. The real value today is in what the deal signals. Nvidia isn't just winning on Earth anymore — it is being chosen first for a market that hasn't even been built yet.

贾布兰·昆迪

太平洋夏令时间 2026 年 8 月 9 日星期日下午 1:11 阅读 6 分钟

英伟达 (NVDA) 刚刚扩大了对人工智能 (AI) 计算的控制，计划进入芯片制造商从未涉足的领域：轨道。 8 月 4 日，SpaceX (SPCX) 和 Nvidia 宣布他们正在合作为 Starmind AI1 卫星设计计算有效载荷，该卫星将使用 Nvidia 的最新硬件在太空运行繁重的人工智能工作负载。 该计划不是一次性的。 SpaceX 概述了一个长期愿景，最终可能扩展到多达 100 万颗人工智能卫星。 这些卫星一起将作为一个环绕地球的巨型数据中心。

对于 Nvidia 来说，除了壮观的场面之外，更引人注目的是这种合作伙伴关系背后的承诺。 SpaceX首席执行官埃隆·马斯克直言，该公司已同意独家使用Nvidia GPU，因为“Vera Rubin架构是最好的架构”。 这是一种最强烈的认可，特别是因为它来自于一个完全有理由构建自己的芯片或寻找替代品的客户。

为什么这对 Nvidia 很重要

这笔交易还显示了英伟达最新举措取得进展的速度有多快。 当该公司在三月份推出其太空计算平台时，它指定了六个合作伙​​伴，而 SpaceX 并不是其中之一。 仅仅几个月后，世界上最雄心勃勃的航天公司现在也签约了。

此新闻的核心硬件是 Nvidia 的 Vera Rubin 平台。 该公司表示，其在轨人工智能性能是其 H100 芯片的 25 倍。 这很重要，因为机会可能是巨大的。 Futurum Research 估计，在星舰发射成本下降和地面数据中心电力限制的推动下，到 2030 年，轨道计算可能会成为一个价值 1 万亿美元的市场。 如果这种情况发生，英伟达将成为主要受益者。

将计算转移到太空背后的逻辑比听起来更实用。 地球上的人工智能数据中心正在遭遇电力、土地和冷却方面的严格限制。 在轨道上，卫星免费获得持续的太阳能和自然冷却，避免了地球上数据中心的瓶颈。

对于英伟达投资者来说，短期回报很小。 太空芯片要到今年晚些时候才能发货，而拥有 100 万颗卫星的网络还有很长的路要走。 今天的真正价值在于交易所传达的信号。 英伟达不再只是在地球上获胜——它正在成为一个尚未建成的市场的首选。
